master_file: 16 - 12 X 4 Feet - Nonlit - AL MADEENA POOJA STORE.cdr
derived_from: tools/agarpathi_structure_probe.py (batch COM structure probe over all 53 landscape Agarpathi boards) + tools/agarpathi_family_a_batch.py (rule-engine run over the 40 Family A, non-tiling boards) + tools/agarpathi_portrait_batch.py (phase 3: rule-engine run, with real-file COM dumps, over all 9 portrait/square boards) - see backend/dataset_analysis/inventory/agarpathi_phase2/structure_probe.json and dataset_analysis/validation/agarpathi/validation_report.json for the raw evidence.
note: This file is classification METADATA only - it has no 'panel_sequence' or 'groups' key, so app.layout.load_brand_rule() loading it has NO effect on compute_layout's tiling/placement path (that code only ever looks for those two specific keys). No geometric placement rule is added here because none is justified by the evidence gathered so far: (1) no tiled Agarpathi board has been generated-and-compared against a real file yet (only 1 of 53 landscape boards, '21 - 11 X 6 Feet', would even trigger tiling per app.layout._tile_plan, and it was deliberately left out of this phase's scope); a rule for a regime with zero real comparisons would be pure fabrication. (2) Even for the validated non-tiling Family A regime, the failure mode found is NOT a 'which sub-element repeats' tiling puzzle the way dalmia's panel_sequence rule solves - it is the plain per-object scale+centre path landing meaningfully off from the designer's hand-placed logo positions across a wide range of real target sizes (median position/size error ~380mm - see app/confidence_bounds.json['agarpathi']). Dalmia's own experience (see CLAUDE.md 'Per-brand tiling rule attempt') is that a rule built from limited cluster/size matching can make results WORSE, not better; writing an equivalent rule here from an even smaller evidence base (no repeated-panel structure exists to derive a rule from at all) is not defensible. If this brand needs a placement improvement, the next step is the same kind of careful, evidence-first process dalmia went through (cluster/size analysis against several real files at each target aspect) - not a rule invented ahead of that analysis.

family_a_single_bitmap.description: 1 embedded product-photo bitmap; page background is a full-page shape (rectangle OR curve - the literal shape type is cosmetic and does not affect app.layout.detect_role's >=90%-page-area bg heuristic). Same 3 logo groups as the master (an 8-curve+4-subgroup badge with its own text, a 10-curve+4-subgroup icon, a 5-curve icon) in every sampled file. This is the master's own structure - compute_layout's generic per-object scale+centre path is at least structurally applicable to these boards (it does not need to invent or drop any bitmap the master lacks), though see 'note' above for its measured accuracy.
family_a_single_bitmap.note_on_count: 39 here = the 41 total Family A landscape boards found by the structure probe, minus the master itself and the same-page-size sanity check ('72'), which were excluded from the accuracy stats as trivial identity cases, not because they are a different family.

family_b_multi_bitmap.description: 2-3 embedded bitmaps (vs. the master's 1) with the same 3 logo groups still present. A genuinely different composition, not a resize of the master - the current engine cannot reproduce these because it has no source for the extra bitmap(s); this is a missing-asset problem, not a geometry problem, and no placement rule fixes it.

family_b_multi_bitmap.outlier_within_family_b: '31 - 35 X 4 Feet' has 80 shapes (vs. the usual ~41-48) and only 2 bitmaps, not 3 - this is the dataset's most extreme landscape aspect ratio (~8.75) and looks like the designer's own duplicated/tiled composition (consistent with the already-documented 35x4ft Agarpathi tiling example in CLAUDE.md 'Designer dataset analysis'), not a plain Family B variant. Flagged, not specially handled.

family_c_no_bitmap.description: No embedded bitmap at all. Originally flagged phase-2 with only 1 landscape sample ('34 - 68 X 65 Inch', a near-square 1.05 aspect) and left unclassified pending more evidence. Phase 3 (see 'portrait_square_findings' below) supplied that evidence: all 9 real portrait/square Agarpathi files ALSO have zero bitmaps, for 10 total samples. This is now a well-supported, real pattern, not a single-sample guess: the designer consistently drops the product-photo bitmap once a board approaches square or goes portrait.
files: 34 - 68 X 65 Inch - Nonlit - SAKTHIVEL STORE.cdr (landscape, near-square 1.05 aspect)
family_c_no_bitmap.action: structurally characterized (no placement rule - see 'portrait_square_findings'): this is a missing-asset problem (no bitmap to place at all) compounded by a full compositional reflow (see below), neither of which a geometric placement rule fixes.

portrait_square_findings.summary: Every one of the 9 real portrait/square Agarpathi boards drops the master's product-photo bitmap AND completely reflows the remaining elements from the master's horizontal (left-text / right-photo, graphics spread across the middle) arrangement into a vertical stack: both shopname texts (Tamil + English) move to the TOP of the page, centered, and the 3 logo/graphic groups move to the BOTTOM half, arranged as one larger centered graphic flanked by two smaller ones. Confirmed by direct shape-position inspection of the cached real dump for '27 - 3 X 4 Feet' (see dataset_analysis/real_dumps_cache/agarpathi/) - not inferred from geometry diffs alone.
portrait_square_findings.shape_count_signature: ~30 non-group leaf shapes for the 8 single-panel portrait/square boards (vs. the landscape master's ~30 non-group leaves too, MINUS its 1 bitmap PLUS 1 extra text line) - i.e. the same ~23 logo curves and 2 background rectangles survive, the bitmap is simply gone, and one more text line appears (likely filling the space the photo used to occupy). '37 - 2 X 6 Feet' has ~2x this (57 shapes, 46 curves, 8 texts) - it is real, designer-made VERTICAL tiling, and app.layout._tile_plan independently predicts this exact board would tile on the y-axis with n=2, matching CLAUDE.md's already-documented '2x6ft board... stacks the panel twice, vertically' finding for this same file.
portrait_square_findings.engine_result: All 9 boards FAIL badly against the current engine (65-71% max diff for 8 of them; '41 - 4 X 8 Inch' is a distinct, more extreme failure - only 1 of 30 objects could even be matched, because at that near-business-card target size (101.6x203.2mm) the designer did not proportionally shrink the master's elements further, breaking the matcher's same-size-bucket gate - flagged as its own outlier, not folded into the headline numbers). Content check is CONTENT_OK on all 9 (text-writing is unaffected by geometry). This is expected, not a new bug: the engine has no mechanism to drop an element or reflow a composition - it only scales/centres what the master already has.
portrait_square_findings.verdict: Orientation-shift rules are NOT the right fix here, and MANUAL is the correct status for all portrait/square Agarpathi requests pending a brand-specific portrait template. Reasoning: (1) this isn't a repositioning problem a 'rotate/reflow the landscape layout' rule could solve - an entire asset (the bitmap) is missing from the target composition, which no geometric transform can supply; (2) the vertical stack (text-block-over-graphics-block) is a distinct, deliberately hand-designed layout, not a rotated/transposed version of the landscape one - building a rule for it would mean designing a second layout engine for this one orientation, which is exactly the kind of un-evidenced, ahead-of-analysis rule this project has already decided against for landscape (see 'note' above); (3) there is no per-shape correspondence between the master's bitmap-inclusive composition and the portrait files' bitmap-free one for a rule to be derived from at the same rigor dalmia's panel_sequence work used. A future portrait-specific master (built by the design team specifically for this orientation, matching the missing-bitmap + top-text/bottom-graphics pattern found here) is the defensible next step, not a geometric rule bolted onto the existing landscape master.
portrait_square_findings.confidence_system_gap_found_and_fixed: app.confidence.confidence_label used a bare aspect-ratio range (max/min, orientation-agnostic) to decide whether a request was 'inside validated territory'. Live-tested against these 9 boards, 4 of them (aspect 1.32-2.00) fell numerically inside the untiled regime's [1.2, 6.5] range - which was derived ENTIRELY from landscape data - and incorrectly came back REVIEW instead of MANUAL, despite zero portrait/square evidence existing. Fixed in app/confidence.py by adding an explicit 'orientation' field to each regime (landscape/portrait/square, only enforced when present, so old synthetic-bounds unit tests are unaffected) and rejecting a request whose orientation doesn't match the regime's - all 9 portrait/square boards now correctly return MANUAL. Verified: all 240 existing backend tests still pass.

known_matching_tooling_gap: tools/validate_all.py's greedy nearest-centre matcher can cross-pair Agarpathi's two separate shopname text objects (Tamil + English name are always two distinct shapes here, unlike dalmia's typically-single shopname shape) when both are classified role='shopname'. Confirmed on the master-regenerated-as-itself identity check: every other of 29 matched objects differed by exactly 0.0mm, but the shopname pair alone showed a spurious ~1600mm 'difference' equal to the real on-page distance between the two text boxes. This inflates any 'shopname_diff_pct_max'/'max_diff' figure that happens to hinge on the shopname role for this brand; the geometric bounds recorded in app/confidence_bounds.json['agarpathi'] exclude the shopname role for this reason. Not fixed here (a tooling/methodology issue in validate_all.py's matcher, out of scope for this phase) - content_check.py's exact-text check remains the only verified signal for shopname correctness in the meantime.
